comparison: Perfect match on claims C26-C29 regarding non-multiplicative AMPAergic scaling. Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval provides detailed experimental justification while peer reviewer acknowledges this as background context that contrasts with GABAergic scaling.

Perfect match on claims C43-C49 regarding optogenetic stimulation methods and activity measurements. Both evaluations support these technical findings. OpenEval notes methodological justifications and limitations; peer reviewer implicitly supports via editor's statement about 'solid data.'
Perfect match on claim C68 regarding lack of frequency changes in bicuculline experiments. Both evaluations support this negative result without challenge.

Perfect match on claims C106-C108 regarding methodological strengths and limitations. Both evaluations support these methodological descriptions and acknowledge culture system limitations appropriately.

High overlap on claims C65-C66, C69-C70, C82 regarding bicuculline upscaling. OpenEval finds strong support; peer reviewer expresses uncertainty, noting 'highly variable' spiking induction with 'robust' synaptic changes across all cells, questioning whether spiking is the primary trigger.

High overlap on claims C31-C35 regarding TTX and CNQX effects on activity. Both evaluations support the activity measurements. OpenEval notes interpretive complications from CNQX's partial spike recovery; peer reviewer notes these differential effects create challenges for conclusions about spiking as trigger.

Partial overlap on claims C38-C39 regarding multiplicative GABAergic scaling. Both evaluations support this finding. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of scaling ratio plots; peer reviewer explicitly confirms 'true scaling (a proportional change to all synapses on a cell) is occurring.'

Moderate overlap on claims C50-C52, C54, C56 regarding optogenetic rescue preventing GABAergic scaling. OpenEval finds strong support for spiking-dependent mechanism; peer reviewer expresses uncertainty, noting TTX and CNQX cause 'identical changes in mIPSC amplitude but have different effects on spiking,' concluding 'more will need to be done.'

Moderate overlap on claims C57-C59, C62, C64 regarding CTZ upscaling. OpenEval supports multiplicative upscaling; peer reviewer raises concern that 'CTZ had a minimal effect on spiking but a large effect on mIPSCs,' contradicting the claim that GABAergic scaling follows spiking.

Moderate overlap on claims C71-C72, C88 regarding dissociation between AMPAergic and GABAergic scaling. Both evaluations support this key finding. OpenEval emphasizes differential effects in same system; peer reviewer calls it 'novel and exciting' but cautions about comparing to different forms of HSP in prior work.

Moderate overlap on claims C85-C87 regarding dissociation of GABAergic from AMPAergic scaling mechanisms. Both evaluations support this conceptual advance. OpenEval emphasizes synthesis with prior work; peer reviewer confirms novelty but urges caution in comparisons.

Partial overlap on claims C4-C5, C23-C24, C75 regarding main conclusions about spike-rate dependent GABAergic scaling. OpenEval finds strong support but notes overstatement; peer reviewer supports multiplicative scaling but expresses uncertainty about spiking as the homeostat.

Partial overlap on claims C5, C76-C77 regarding spiking-dependent mechanism. OpenEval supports conclusions from collective evidence; peer reviewer expresses uncertainty, noting data details 'may suggest that spiking is not the (or the only) homeostat.'

Partial overlap on claims C99, C105, C109 regarding overarching conclusions about GABAergic scaling's homeostatic role. OpenEval supports but notes overstatement; peer reviewer raises critical temporal concern about time course alignment and whether cells would eventually recover, questioning causal claims.

Minimal overlap on claim C84 regarding timing of GABAergic scaling before activity recovery. OpenEval finds correlative support; peer reviewer raises major concern that only 24h timepoint was measured for synaptic changes, making it 'not yet possible to conclude how the time courses align.'

Minimal overlap on claim C80 regarding dissociation between AMPAergic and GABAergic mechanisms. OpenEval supports this critical finding; peer reviewer questions it based on CTZ data showing minimal spiking effect but large mIPSC effect.
